title: Manaslu vs Annapurna Circuit: Which Trek to Choose
meta_description: Manaslu vs Annapurna Circuit compared: Larkya La 5,106 m vs Thorong La 5,416 m, roads, crowds, permits, guide rules, cost, days and who each trek suits.
summary: Choose the Manaslu Circuit for quieter trails, fewer roads, Tibetan Buddhist villages and a wilder feel, accepting a restricted area permit, a mandatory guide and simpler lodges. Choose the Annapurna Circuit for more comfort, more flexibility, a higher pass at Thorong La and easy road and flight exits, accepting jeep traffic and busier lodges.

sections.heading: The two circuits side by side
paras: The Manaslu and Annapurna circuits are neighbours. Both loop around a massif of 8,000 m peaks, both cross a high pass above 5,000 m, and they even meet: the Manaslu Circuit ends at Dharapani, which is a stop on the Annapurna Circuit. Yet they feel very different on the ground. The table below sums up the main differences for a typical itinerary from Kathmandu.

sections.heading: Mountains and scenery
paras: On the Manaslu Circuit the mountains come close. From Lho, Samagaun and Bimthang you look straight at Manaslu, 8,163 m, with its glaciers spilling into the valley, and Himal Chuli and Ngadi Chuli rise above Shyala. The lower Budhi Gandaki is a deep gorge with waterfalls and suspension bridges, and the forest descent from Bimthang is among the wildest on any popular trek.

The Annapurna Circuit offers a broader sweep: Annapurna II, Annapurna III and Gangapurna above Manang, the Tilicho area, Thorong La at 5,416 m and then the dry, Tibetan-style Kali Gandaki valley around Muktinath and Jomsom. Its variety of landscapes is hard to beat. Manaslu is more concentrated and dramatic; Annapurna is longer and more varied.

sections.heading: Villages and culture
paras: Both treks pass from Hindu and mixed communities in the lower valleys to Tibetan Buddhist communities higher up. On Manaslu the change happens at Namrung, and the Nubri villages of Lho, Samagaun and Samdo feel little changed by tourism, with monasteries such as Ribung Gompa and Samdo's families of Tibetan origin. Adding the Tsum Valley takes you deeper still, into a valley that opened to foreigners only in 2008.

The Annapurna Circuit's culture is equally rich, with Manang, Braga Gompa, the pilgrimage site of Muktinath and the Thakali villages of the Kali Gandaki. But decades of trekking and the arrival of roads mean villages here are more geared to visitors, with bakeries, cafés and souvenir shops.

sections.heading: Roads, crowds and atmosphere
paras: The biggest change over the past fifteen years has been road building. On the Annapurna side jeeps now reach Manang, and on the western side a road runs from Muktinath through Jomsom to Pokhara. Trekkers can avoid much of the road using alternative trails, but dust and traffic are part of the experience. On Manaslu the road ends at Machha Khola for most of the year and the trail above Jagat remains a footpath, though construction is moving north.

Numbers are also very different. The restricted area permit, compulsory guide and higher cost keep Manaslu quieter, even in October. You still meet other groups in Samagaun and at Dharamsala, but rarely the crowds of Manang or Thorong Phedi. If solitude matters, Manaslu wins.

sections.heading: Difficulty and altitude
paras: Thorong La is higher than Larkya La by about 300 m, and its high camp sits close to 4,850 m. Larkya La is lower but often feels just as hard, because the crossing day from Dharamsala to Bimthang is long, 8 to 10 hours, with a steep 1,500 m descent and fewer facilities. Both treks need acclimatisation days, typically in Manang on the Annapurna side and Samagaun on the Manaslu side.

Lodges on Manaslu are simpler and colder, with fewer attached bathrooms and less choice of food, and the remote setting makes evacuation slower. For first-time trekkers, the Annapurna Circuit is the gentler introduction; for those with some experience, Manaslu is a natural next step.

sections.heading: How the itineraries compare
paras: On paper the two treks take similar time, but the shape of the walking differs. Manaslu starts low, at Machha Khola, 930 m, and has no road above it, so you walk every day from the second day to the end. On the Annapurna side most groups now drive to Chame or even Manang and walk only the high section, which shortens the trek to 9–12 days but also shortens the time your body has to adjust. The table compares the key stages.

The practical result is that both treks give similar acclimatisation if you follow a good plan, but Manaslu enforces it because there is no road to cut it short. Annapurna rewards discipline: driving straight to Manang and crossing Thorong La four days later is possible, and it is a common cause of altitude problems on the Circuit.

Side trips differ too. From the Manaslu trail you can add the Tsum Valley, about 6–7 extra days, a long day hike to Manaslu Base Camp at about 4,800 m, or Birendra Tal near Samagaun. From Manang you can add Tilicho Lake at 4,919 m in 2–3 days, the Ice Lake day hike above Braga, or the restricted Nar Phu valley in 4–5 days.

sections.heading: Permits, guides, lodges and cost
paras: Rooms on both treks are cheap, often NPR 500–1,500 a night, because owners expect you to eat dinner and breakfast where you sleep. Food is where the difference shows. Manang has bakeries, cafés with espresso machines and long menus, and prices stay moderate because jeeps bring supplies. On Manaslu everything above Jagat arrives by mule or porter, menus are shorter and a plate of dal bhat costs roughly NPR 800–1,200 in Samagaun and more at Dharamsala. Budget about US$ 30–40 a day for food and lodging on Manaslu against US$ 25–35 on the Annapurna side.

Hot showers, phone charging and Wi-Fi are available at most Annapurna Circuit lodges, often for a small fee. On Manaslu, solar or gas showers are common up to Samagaun, charging can cost NPR 200–500 per device higher up, and Wi-Fi is patchy above Namrung. Carry a power bank and enough Nepali rupees in cash, as there are no ATMs on either trail above the road heads.

Manaslu needs the restricted area permit, issued only through registered agencies and charged by the week and day, plus the Manaslu and Annapurna conservation area permits and a local fee. A licensed guide is compulsory. Since 2026, as we understand it, solo trekkers can obtain the permit without a partner. The Annapurna Circuit needs the Annapurna Conservation Area Permit, and Nepal's 2023 rules require foreign trekkers to use a licensed guide in most areas, though enforcement has varied; check current status before you travel.
These differences explain the price gap. A 14-day Manaslu Circuit with a reputable agency usually costs US$1,100 to 1,600, compared with US$800 to 1,300 for a similar Annapurna Circuit.

sections.heading: Which one should you choose
paras: Many trekkers end up doing both, in different years, or even back to back by continuing from Dharapani up the Annapurna Circuit to Manang and Thorong La in about 25 days. If you must choose one, the list below may help.
list: Choose Manaslu if you want quiet trails, few roads, close views of an 8,000 m peak and Tibetan Buddhist villages with little tourism.
Choose Manaslu if you have trekked before and are happy with simpler lodges and a compulsory guide.
Choose Annapurna if it is your first long trek, you want more lodge comfort and flexibility, or you want to add Tilicho Lake or Muktinath.
Choose Annapurna if budget matters most or you want to exit by flight from Jomsom.
Combine them if you have three to four weeks: Manaslu to Dharapani, then the Annapurna Circuit over Thorong La.

faqs.q: Is Manaslu harder than the Annapurna Circuit?
faqs.a: Overall they are similar. Thorong La is higher at 5,416 m against Larkya La at 5,106 m, but the Manaslu crossing day is long and steep on the descent, lodges are simpler and the route is more remote. Most trekkers rate Manaslu slightly harder because of the remoteness rather than the altitude.

faqs.q: Which is more beautiful, Manaslu or Annapurna?
faqs.a: Both are outstanding. Manaslu gives closer, more concentrated mountain views and wilder valleys with fewer roads. The Annapurna Circuit has greater variety, from Manang's peaks to the dry Kali Gandaki around Muktinath. Photographers seeking solitude often prefer Manaslu.

faqs.q: Is the Manaslu Circuit less crowded than Annapurna?
faqs.a: Yes, much less. The restricted area permit, compulsory guide and higher cost limit numbers, and there are fewer lodges. You will meet other groups in October, especially in Samagaun and Dharamsala, but not the crowds of Manang or Thorong Phedi.

faqs.q: Can I combine the Manaslu and Annapurna circuits?
faqs.a: Yes. The Manaslu Circuit ends at Dharapani on the Annapurna Circuit. From there you can walk on to Chame, Manang and Thorong La to Muktinath, adding about 8 to 10 days. You need the Manaslu permits plus the Annapurna Conservation Area Permit for the whole Annapurna section.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for the Annapurna Circuit?
faqs.a: Nepal's 2023 rules require foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide in most trekking areas, including Annapurna, though enforcement has varied in practice. On Manaslu the guide is strictly enforced through the restricted area permit. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which trek is better for first-timers?
faqs.a: The Annapurna Circuit is usually better for first-timers, with more lodges, better food choice, easier exits by road or flight and more flexibility to rest. Fit beginners can do Manaslu too, with a good itinerary and two nights in Samagaun.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper, Manaslu or Annapurna Circuit?
faqs.a: The Annapurna Circuit is cheaper, typically US$800 to 1,300 with an agency against US$1,100 to 1,600 for Manaslu. The difference comes mainly from Manaslu's restricted area permit and mandatory guide, plus higher food prices in its remote upper villages.

faqs.q: Which has better views of 8,000 m peaks?
faqs.a: Manaslu, because you walk right below an 8,000 m peak for several days. The Annapurna Circuit shows Annapurna I only distantly; its main views are of Annapurna II, III, IV and Gangapurna, all below 8,000 m, plus Dhaulagiri from the Kali Gandaki side.

faqs.q: Which trek has more roads now?
faqs.a: The Annapurna Circuit, by far. Jeep roads run up the Marsyangdi towards Manang and down the Kali Gandaki from Muktinath. On Manaslu the road reaches Machha Khola and sometimes Jagat; above that the route is still a footpath, although construction is moving north.
